strings.intro: Say what you did with the tool and what the work is, and this writes the line you need: a citation, a credit, or a note. Everything stays on this page.
strings.use: What did you do with it?
strings.prompt: What you asked it, in a few words
strings.promptHint: MLA uses this as the title of the entry. Keep it short and exact.
strings.credit: Credit line, on the work itself
strings.note: A note in your own words
strings.comment: A comment at the top of the file
strings.none: Nothing is required for this. A note in your own files is still a good habit.
strings.sources: Cite the sources you used, as themselves. The tool is not the source; it is how you found them. If you want to say that, use the note below.
strings.reviewed: Formats follow the MLA Style Center's guidance on generative AI. Check your school's own rule as well; it may ask for more.

uses.label: Used an image, sound or video it made
Used its ideas, outline or structure
Had it edit, fix grammar or translate
Got feedback from it on my draft

works.label: A poster, slides or a display
A worksheet, lesson or assessment (I'm a teacher)

why.words: MLA treats the tool's words like any other source you quote or paraphrase: an entry in the Works Cited, and a short citation where you use them.
why.image: An image is a work, so it gets a Works Cited entry. It also needs a credit where people see it, because a reader of a poster never sees your Works Cited.
why.ideas: If the tool shaped what you argue or how you organised it, that is a source of ideas, and MLA says to cite it. Say in your text where the idea came from.
why.edit: Editing, grammar and translation are what MLA calls functional uses. They do not go in the Works Cited, but they should be acknowledged, in a note or in the text.
why.feedback: Feedback that you acted on shaped the work. It is acknowledged, not cited: the words are still yours.
why.sources: The tool found the sources; it did not write them. Cite each source as itself, and only after you have opened and checked it.
why.teaching: Students are asked to disclose their use. A line at the bottom of the worksheet, and a sentence to the class, is the same rule applied to the person who set it.
why.poster: This is the line students ask for. It takes ten seconds and it is the difference between a poster and a mystery.
why.code: Code is easy to change and easy to review, which is why a comment at the top is enough: it says where it came from and that a person checked it.
why.private: If nobody else sees it, nothing is owed to anyone. Keeping a note of what you did is still useful when you look at the file in a year.
